Chapter 8: The Power of Saying Yes
You know, there’s a quiet kind of magic that happens when you say yes—even when fear is whispering no in your ear.
If you think back, a lot of the biggest turning points in life usually come from those moments when you’re open to something new. Maybe you agreed to audition for something you weren’t sure you could handle, or you accepted a random invitation to collaborate. Sometimes, it’s stepping into a role that feels completely unfamiliar—and honestly, a little terrifying.
For me, the world of improv really drove this lesson home. Picture this: you’re up on stage, and there’s no script, no safety net—just you, your instincts, and your scene partners. The only way forward? Trust yourself, listen closely, and say yes to whatever unfolds.
What’s wild is how that lesson doesn’t just stay on the stage. It spills into real life, too.
I remember one night during an especially chaotic improv show—everything that could go wrong, did. Lines were forgotten, props fell apart, and it felt like the audience was getting restless. But instead of freaking out, the cast leaned in. They embraced the chaos, said yes to the mess, and actually built on each other’s mistakes. Suddenly, what started as a disaster turned into some of the best comedy of the night. The laughter was real, all because everyone was willing to be present and a little vulnerable.
Most of us spend so much energy trying to control outcomes, dodge risks, and avoid looking foolish. But here’s something I’ve noticed: the best moments, the ones that really lead to growth, connection, and joy—they almost always show up when you let go of control and open yourself to possibility.
Now, saying yes doesn’t mean you have to throw caution out the window or ignore your boundaries. It just means being open to the unknown, and trusting that something good might be waiting on the other side of uncertainty.
Approaching life this way opened doors I never expected—like directing for the first time, mentoring younger performers, or diving into projects that felt way out of my depth. Each yes was a leap of faith, and, sure, sometimes things got messy or didn’t work out. But more often than not, saying yes led to discoveries I never would’ve made otherwise.
Looking back, I realize that saying yes became a kind of superpower. It turned roadblocks into adventures, and mistakes into happy little accidents.
Most people don’t realize how much potential is just sitting on the other side of their comfort zone—or how much can change with a single, wholehearted yes.
